title: Introduce replay-driven, drift-resilient canary orchestrator
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a replay-driven canary orchestration service that replays sampled production traces against candidate builds to improve regression signal-to-noise. Integrates with rollout guard to pause and rollback on high-confidence regressions.
description: Context and motivation: Continuous perf canaries detect regressions early, but noisy production signals (traffic bursts, distribution shifts) lead to false positives and noisy alerts. This PR introduces a replay-driven canary orchestrator that captures stratified, anonymized production traces and replays them deterministically against candidate binaries in an isolated harness. The approach reduces false positives by comparing matched workloads, provides deterministic tail latency and throughput deltas, and produces a calibrated confidence score that feeds existing rollout guards. Design summary: - New service 'replay-orchestrator' responsible for trace sampling, anonymization, storage, and scheduling replays. - New probe type 'replay-probe' that runs recorded traces concurrently against baseline (deployed) and candidate (head) environments and aggregates latency/throughput distributions. - Stratified slicing by traffic signature (route, payload size, user cohort) to surface targeted regressions. - Confidence model: bootstrap-based comparison on high-percentile latencies with false-discovery-rate controls. - Integrations: rollout guard API, perf-canary dashboard, tracing/metrics pipeline (prometheus + jaeger), RBAC. Key changes in this PR: - services/replay-orchestrator: new service, scheduler, worker pool (Go). - perf-canary/agents/replay_probe.go: probe implementation and orchestration API. - perf-canary/harness: deterministic replay harness with KV-cache warmup and sequence-control. - observability: dashboards, new metrics (replay_runtime_ms, delta_p95, replay_confidence). - infra: k8s job templates, S3-compatible artifact storage for traces. Testing and validation: - Unit tests for scheduler, probe logic, and confidence model. - Deterministic replay integration tests using recorded synthetic traffic. - Small-scale production shadow run (stage->prod shadow) for two weeks, followed by a staged rollout. - Load tests to verify harness isolation and resource accounting. Rollout plan and safety: - Initial rollout to canary tier only with max 5 concurrent replay probes per cluster. - Auto-pause and open rollback if delta_p95 > 15% with confidence > 0.95 OR throughput drop > 10% and confidence > 0.9. - Manual review gates for high-impact routes. Checklist: - [x] Scheduler + workers implemented - [x] Replay harness deterministic (seeded RNG, KV warmup) - [x] Metrics + dashboards created - [x] CI integration tests added - [x] Security review for trace anonymization - [x] Staged rollout plan documented Related work: builds on ENG-4821 (canary framework refactor) and ENG-5020 (rollout guard API). Known limitations: does not yet support streaming-replay for long-lived sessions; replay storage retention defaults to 7 days configurable per-team.
commits_summary: 3 commits: 1) add replay-orchestrator service and k8s job templates; 2) implement replay_probe and confidence scoring; 3) add dashboards, e2e replay tests, and infra tweaks. Commit messages are compact and focused; total ~3 feature commits + test/infra fixes.
review_comments: Diego Moretti: Overall approach looks strong. A few concerns: how do we ensure replayed traces are representative when payload-dependent routing exists? Also need stronger throttling for expensive replays.

Aisha Patel (author): We added stratified sampling by route and user cohort to address representativeness. Throttling is implemented at the scheduler (max concurrent per-cluster) and we added cost-based backoff in scheduler.go.
Lina Zhang: Please add telemetry to track how often replays change rollout decisions. Also request an opt-out flag for PII-sensitive teams.
Aisha Patel: telemetry added (replay_decision_count, replay_optouts) and an opt-out label was introduced in team config; security review verified anonymization.
Marcus O'Neill: Minor nit on exponential backoff constants and a request to surface confidence threshold as a runtime config.
Aisha Patel: moved thresholds into feature flags + runtime config and updated docs.
Diego Moretti: LGTM after changes. Approved.
ci_checks: bench: warn (high variance on one harness node - rerun succeeded)
merge_summary: Merged after approvals and CI green. Squash commit message: 'replay-driven canary orchestrator: replay probe, scheduler, harness, metrics, tests'
post_merge_actions: Created dashboard in perf-canary team space
Filed follow-up ENG-5102 to add streaming-replay support
Tagged infra team to review k8s job resource limits
notes: This PR intentionally keeps replay artifacts ephemeral by default (7-day retention) and requires team opt-in for longer retention. Security reviewed trace fields; PII hashing applied at capture time. Observability owners: perf-canary on-call.
example_run_summary: Staging replay run (2026-02-18): 1200 traces replayed across 12 slices. Observed median delta_p95 = +4.2% candidate vs baseline, confidence=0.92; flagged 3 slices for manual review, no auto-rollback triggered.
risk_assessment: Medium: adds new long-running worker surface and storage for trace artifacts. Mitigations: strict ACLs, opt-out, per-team quotas, and cost throttling in scheduler.
changelog: 2026-02-15 - initial PR opened; 2026-02-20 - added throttling and opt-out; 2026-02-23 - telemetry + runtime config; 2026-02-24 - merged to main.
